one_line: Incident co-control room where agents investigate and prepare mitigations while authority remains human-gated.
what_it_does: Provides policy-evaluated incident investigation, bounded mitigation staging, human approval, post-check assessment, and independently reviewed memory reuse.
leverage_rationale: Capability sculpting changes the available tool surface as authority moves between agent, operator, application, and reviewer; a general UI-driving agent could not comparably guarantee these boundaries.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes inspect-only start, withdrawal of propose_mitigation after staging, human approval, later post-check assessment, and zero-tool certification page.
Visual packet shows a multi-step dark incident console with prompts, structured outputs, and review/confirmation states.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, unusually complete workflow and visible intermediate states, though most frame text is small and end-to-end observation is claimed rather than directly exercised here.
execution_evidence: 177-second demo transcript covers investigation, policy rejection, staging, approval, post-check, pending memory, and independent review.
Three frame sheets show successive UI states and structured result panels.
impact_rationale: Incident responders and operators have a concrete need for reliable evidence, policy boundaries, and human accountability; the design directly addresses unsafe similarity-based operational reuse.
impact_evidence: Specific checkout-latency incident scenario with version mismatch, failed outcome, tenant/review constraints, and sandboxed mitigation.
Separate measurement, agent assessment, and backend verdict are retained.
creativity_rationale: The capability-sculpting interaction model and separation of investigation, authority, post-check, and certification are a memorable and ambitious use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Tools are deliberately withdrawn at authority boundaries rather than merely exposed as actions.
Independent reviewer page has no WebMCP tools and governed memory cannot self-promote.
usability_note: Structured staged workflow and visible authority boundaries appear usable for operations teams, though the dense console is technical.
red_flags: Demo uses a deterministic isolated simulator rather than production infrastructure.
Frame-sheet text is often too small for detailed visual verification.
standouts: Strongest authority-boundary design in the packet.
Governed evidence is explicitly prevented from becoming future authority without review.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with credible operational impact and a coherent, deeply pursued workflow.

one_line: Shared diagnostic workspace where an agent asks a nearby human for precise physical evidence.
what_it_does: Connects telemetry-based troubleshooting with a bounded human observation, attributes the answer as evidence, and updates diagnostic confidence.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides a structured pending handoff whose human answer resolves into the same investigation state; generic UI automation would be less reliable and less semantically explicit.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies a pending tool call waiting for Open/Partially open/Closed observation.
Evidence timeline attributes sensor, agent, and human observations separately.
execution_rationale: The described greenhouse case and handoff flow are coherent, with frame sheets showing a multi-state diagnostic UI, but there is no submitted video and fine details are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show onboarding, diagnostic workspace, and evidence-oriented states.
About text describes selected Valve V2, human task, resolution, and confidence update.
impact_rationale: Technicians routinely need to combine machine telemetry with physical observations; the product addresses a real boundary that agents cannot cross alone.
impact_evidence: Concrete irrigation fault scenario and constrained physical inspection choices.
Auditable chain distinguishes sensor report, agent inference, and human observation.
creativity_rationale: The precise human-observation handoff is a fresh interaction model, not just a chatbot added to a dashboard.
creativity_evidence: Agent pauses and requests one concrete physical observation rather than pretending to see equipment.
Human answer becomes typed evidence that changes confidence.
usability_note: Small bounded answer set and explicit next action should make the handoff approachable for a nearby technician.
red_flags: No video was submitted.
Execution and WebMCP invocation are supported mainly by description and screenshots.
standouts: Evidence provenance is central to the interaction.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-value collaboration pattern with strong leverage despite limited execution evidence.

one_line: Approval-gated browser control surface for inspecting and coordinating bounded coding-agent work.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect workspace/project/session state, focus sessions, start scoped work, and send feedback through product-level tools reflected in a shared dashboard.
leverage_rationale: Semantic session IDs, repository state, approvals, and bounded results are materially more reliable through WebMCP than pixel automation, while humans retain dashboard visibility and approval control.
leverage_evidence: Seven named tools expose workspace, project, session, focus, start, and feedback concepts.
Description states every state change remains visible in the same dashboard and raw terminal/filesystem power is withheld.
execution_rationale: The product concept and backend-free demo route are coherent, with frame sheets showing dashboard and workflow states, but no video and only one gallery image are available.
execution_evidence: About text claims complete public /webmcp contract and paired real-dashboard integration.
Three frame sheets show dark dashboard, session/task panels, and resulting states.
impact_rationale: Developers coordinating multiple agents have a real fragmentation and safety problem; a shared bounded control surface directly improves inspection and handoff.
impact_evidence: Specific pain points: terminals, repository views, chat threads, session state, and approvals.
Scoped start and feedback tools preserve human oversight.
creativity_rationale: A strong product-level agent interface for coding coordination, though the underlying dashboard/control-room category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Uses WebMCP as a semantic product vocabulary rather than raw browser control.
Human keeps live dashboard and approval context while agent operates bounded sessions.
usability_note: The bounded tool vocabulary and visible shared dashboard should reduce ambiguity for both developers and agents.
red_flags: No submitted video.
Real authenticated bridge is described but the public demo is backend-free.
standouts: Good semantic replacement for brittle UI-driving in coding-agent coordination.
advance_reason: Strong practical WebMCP leverage and credible developer impact; execution evidence is thinner than top entries.

one_line: Agent-assisted job search and application workspace with human-controlled drafting, validation, and submission.
what_it_does: Supports job discovery, profile matching, application drafts, validation, submission, and status tracking through a React frontend with local persistence and WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured job/application workflows are more dependable than scraping and clicking, but the same outcomes remain possible through ordinary UI automation with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description lists structured search, compare, draft, validate, and tracking workflows.
Local UI and agent tools use the same workflows and separate read-only from state-changing actions.
execution_rationale: The claimed end-to-end journey is plausible but there are no gallery images or video frames, so execution is capped by thin evidence.
execution_evidence: About text claims a complete application journey and browser localStorage persistence.
Facts report live demo but no visual evidence packet.
impact_rationale: Job seekers face repetitive, fragmented applications and benefit materially from search, drafting, validation, and tracking in one workspace.
impact_evidence: Specific candidate workflow and stated pain points.
Human remains in control before consequential application submission.
creativity_rationale: A competent agent-native synthesis of an established job platform category, with human-in-control workflow as the main new angle.
creativity_evidence: One connected candidate/agent workflow spanning discovery through tracking.
Structured validation before submission.
usability_note: A unified workflow should reduce application fragmentation, but no visual evidence is available to assess polish.
red_flags: No screenshots beyond packaging and no video frames.
Frontend prototype/local persistence limits evidence of durable real-world application submission.
standouts: Clear candidate value proposition and sensible human approval boundary.
advance_reason: Potentially useful, but evidence is too thin and concept is less differentiated than stronger entries.

one_line: Browser-native launch command center that plans, recovers, and exports an approved event runbook.
what_it_does: Plans a launch across venue, menu, budget, invites, timeline, then recovers from a sponsor surge and generates connected handoff artifacts.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured state, bounded planning tools, injected surprise, recovery, approval, and multi-format handoff make the agent workflow substantially more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies plan/recovery under fixed budget and preserved menu constraints.
Tools register on the page and expose connected outputs including Calendar, ICS, email, Slack Block Kit, and automation JSON.
execution_rationale: The scope is ambitious and the frame sheets show many planning/output states, but there is no video and the repository is not public for deeper corroboration.
execution_evidence: Seven gallery/frame panels show a polished command-center progression.
About text describes surprise injection, recovery, approval, runbook export, and handoff.
impact_rationale: Event planners and launch coordinators can benefit from constraint-preserving planning and connected handoffs, though the demo scenario is more illustrative than essential.
impact_evidence: Concrete launch-night planning workflow with budget and dietary constraints.
Exported artifacts target multiple real coordination channels.
creativity_rationale: The surprise-event recovery challenge plus connected cross-channel handoff is ambitious, memorable, and deeply aligned with agent work in stateful tools.
creativity_evidence: Injects a sponsor VIP surge after initial planning and requires constraint-preserving recovery.
Generates linked outputs across calendar, ICS, email, Slack, and automation formats.
usability_note: The command-center framing and approval staging appear accessible, though the breadth may increase cognitive load.
red_flags: No submitted video.
Static/no-backend demo means integrations are output artifacts rather than live external changes.
standouts: Excellent recovery scenario and ambitious handoff design.
advance_reason: Highly creative and well-scoped demonstration of stateful agent planning and recovery.

one_line: Shared study board where a student and agent manage tasks, alarms, quizzes, focus, and progress.
what_it_does: Combines task board, alarms, flashcards, quiz area, focus timer, streak/XP dashboard, and live progress charts with agent actions through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets the agent act on the same study board and trigger concrete functions such as tasks and alarms, but general UI automation could achieve similar results with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly lists shared live state and agent/user parity across tasks, alarms, timer, and progress.
Single packaging screenshot is the only visual evidence.
execution_rationale: The feature set is coherent but evidence is limited to a packaging screenshot and demo status is unknown; end-to-end completion is not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: About text claims multiple integrated study features and browser-local behavior.
Facts report no frame sheets and demo_alive unknown.
impact_rationale: Students have a clear need for planning, focus, practice, and feedback; the shared board can reduce friction between intention and action.
impact_evidence: Specific study workflow features including alarms, quizzes, timer, and progress.
Human and agent share the same board rather than a separate chatbot.
creativity_rationale: A sensible agent-native study workspace with shared state, but most individual features are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent can perform concrete study actions instead of only explaining them.
Live streak/XP and progress views connect actions into one workspace.
usability_note: The feature breadth is useful, but the lack of observable demo evidence prevents confident polish assessment.
red_flags: No frame sheets or video.
Demo availability is unknown; claims are largely descriptive.
standouts: Good shared-state framing for human/agent study support.
advance_reason: Useful concept but insufficient evidence and limited novelty relative to stronger submissions.

one_line: 3D science-fiction escape room that benchmarks agents through structured exploration and evidence-based solving.
what_it_does: Lets humans and agents explore a deterministic facility, inspect and collect clues, unlock rooms, reconstruct a mystery, and submit a supported solution through 21 WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: The structured world-state and action tools make agent exploration, evidence gathering, and verified end states possible in a way generic UI driving would be markedly less reliable.
leverage_evidence: 21 tools expose rooms, spatial state, observations, movement, inventory, clues, codes, and final escape.
Description says tools reveal only legitimately knowable information rather than hidden solution state.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets visibly show a 3D environment, lobby, rankings, and report-card states, supporting a real scoped benchmark, though no video is submitted.
execution_evidence: Five gallery images include 3D facility and agent-performance/reporting views.
Deterministic mystery and five interconnected locations are described.
impact_rationale: The benchmark addresses a meaningful gap in evaluating agents on situated investigation, tool use, evidence linkage, and verified completion; it also offers legitimate play value.
impact_evidence: Specific benchmark question and measurable report-card metrics.
Mission requires cross-location evidence and supported final theory rather than text-only answer.
creativity_rationale: A playable 3D mystery designed as an agent benchmark is a striking and ambitious interaction model with depth beyond a tool demo.
creativity_evidence: Combines human navigable 3D world, deterministic mystery engine, and constrained agent tools.
Verified end state and performance rankings make the experience evaluative and replayable.
usability_note: The explicit action vocabulary helps agents, while the 3D environment is engaging for humans; complexity may raise onboarding cost.
red_flags: No video submitted.
Agent interaction claims are not directly shown in a video packet.
standouts: Memorable benchmark/game hybrid with strong structured-world leverage.
advance_reason: High creativity and leverage with credible visible product packaging and a distinctive benchmark purpose.

one_line: App Store screenshot localization desk where agents write, translate, validate, and export overlay copy.
what_it_does: Loads iOS screens, applies headline/subhead templates, switches locales, checks real export-canvas overflow, respects human locks, and exports production PNG ZIPs.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates structured copy, locale, overflow, lock, and export semantics against the live canvas; pixel automation would be fragile for repeated localization and validation.
leverage_evidence: Named tools include get_page_state, set_overlay, set_template, add_locale, check_overflow, and export_zip.
Lock errors prevent agents from overwriting human-approved frames; overflow is measured against 1320x2868 export.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets show a coherent studio workflow from screens and copy to localization/overflow/export states, with a clear no-login sample setup.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show canvas/editor, copy and locale states, and export-oriented results.
Description specifies three preloaded sample screens, templates, locks, overflow, and ZIP export.
impact_rationale: App teams and marketers have a concrete repetitive localization and screenshot-production problem; the tool addresses quality failures before store submission.
impact_evidence: Specific production workflow and real App Store export dimensions.
Human owns pixels/lock/ship while agent handles copy, translation, and overflow checks.
creativity_rationale: The two-player division of labor between human visual authority and agent copy/localization is a focused, original WebMCP application.
creativity_evidence: Samples are immediately operable and agent can complete a localization pass from first visit.
Campaign template infers marketing graphic type from product-slide copy.
usability_note: Preloaded samples, explicit locks, bounded tools, and one-desk workflow make the product unusually approachable.
red_flags: Visual evidence is frame-sheet based rather than a narrated video.
No backend is used, so export is local artifact generation.
standouts: Excellent narrow workflow fit and human/agent role clarity.
Concrete overflow validation is more than copy generation.
advance_reason: Strong practical leverage, polished workflow, and clear audience value.

one_line: Shared launch-planning workspace for configuring a constrained voice-agent front desk with owner approval.
what_it_does: Collects business inputs, calculates missed-call opportunity and coverage, drafts a constrained call policy, and presents an auditable plan for human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured calculations, editable shared state, and visible activity ledger improve reliability over UI automation, but the workflow remains feasible through ordinary form driving.
leverage_evidence: Six described tools read/update inputs, calculate risk, recommend coverage, draft policy, and open review.
Final approval, deployment, purchasing, calling, and messaging are deliberately not tools.
execution_rationale: The concept is coherent and bounded, but no gallery images or video frames were submitted, so execution evidence is thin.
execution_evidence: About text specifies inputs, deterministic calculations, policy draft, ledger, and local save.
Facts report no video and zero gallery images.
impact_rationale: Local-service businesses lose revenue from missed calls and need constrained setup before deploying consequential automation; the intended audience and value are clear.
impact_evidence: Specific industry, call-volume, missed-call-rate, job-value, and coverage inputs.
Owner retains personal approval and demo confirms no external system changes.
creativity_rationale: The owner/agent split and explicit no-deployment boundary are thoughtful, though the planning workflow is a familiar business-assistant pattern.
creativity_evidence: Agent drafts a constrained call policy while owner approves and saves.
Visible activity ledger makes the handoff auditable.
usability_note: Simple business inputs and deterministic outputs should be accessible, but visual usability cannot be assessed from the packet.
red_flags: No screenshot evidence beyond packaging and no video.
No external deployment is demonstrated; only local save is claimed.
standouts: Good consequential-action boundary and clear small-business audience.
advance_reason: Credible niche impact, but execution evidence is insufficient and WebMCP delta is moderate.

one_line: Collaborative circuit schematic workbench with visual editing and agent-native authoring, highlighting, and SPICE simulation.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect circuit state, author validated graphs, highlight components in the human schematic, and simulate exact circuit snapshots with measured outputs.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides precise circuit graph semantics, optimistic project hashes, shared visual highlighting, and simulation tied to exact snapshots; pixel automation is poorly suited to CAD authoring and measured verification.
leverage_evidence: Four named tools cover inspect, validated complete graph authoring, human-visible highlighting, and ngspice simulation.
Workflow changes emitter resistor and reruns simulation to explain measured tradeoffs.
execution_rationale: The described beta-100 bias-stage workflow is coherent and the frame sheets show schematic/editor and simulation states, but demo status is unknown and no video is submitted.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show visual circuit workbench, highlighted design, and simulation/result states.
About text describes complete circuit creation, measured node voltages/currents, edit, and rerun.
impact_rationale: Circuit designers and learners need a shared visual source of truth plus precise simulation/explanation; the tool addresses both collaboration and verification.
impact_evidence: Concrete beta-100 NPN bias design and stability/headroom comparison.
Simulation results are tied to exact circuit snapshot and remain visible to the human.
creativity_rationale: The dual-native-interface model for visual CAD and agent graph operations is original, technically ambitious, and pursued through validation, highlighting, and measurement.
creativity_evidence: Optimistic project hash guards shared edits.
Agent-authored circuit is highlighted in the same human-visible schematic and simulated with ngspice.
usability_note: Shared visual circuit and precise agent actions are promising, though CAD complexity remains for novices.
red_flags: Demo availability is unknown.
No submitted video; evidence relies on frame sheets and description.
standouts: Excellent fit between WebMCP structure and circuit semantics.
Measured simulation closes the loop beyond diagram generation.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated technical workflow with transformative WebMCP leverage and credible impact.
